posts.fact_source: FIP Reglamento de Juego, Regla 13.1.l (own glass allowed, own fence = point lost)

slides.q: Hit your own fence to get it over?
slides.claim: Your shot hits your own fence, then goes over the net.

slides.text: Off your own fence, then over the net.

scene.alt: Side view: the ball hits the player's own fence above the back glass and flies over the net

slides.line:
Own back glass: fine.
Own fence: point **lost**.

posts.caption:
Your own back glass is your friend. But what about the fence above it? 🤔

Most club players get this one wrong.

Comment FAIR or FAULT before you swipe 👇 Send it to the one who always argues.
Follow @fairorfault – your daily padel quiz.

posts.fact_source: FIP Reglamento, La Pala: cabeza grosor máximo 38 mm, largo total máx. 45,5 cm, ancho máx. 26 cm

slides.q: How thick may your racket be?
slides.claim: Your racket may be up to 38 mm thick.

slides.text: Your racket may be up to 38 mm thick.

posts.caption:
Thick, thin, teardrop, round – rackets look very different. But the rules set hard limits. 📏

Length, width and thickness are all capped.

Did you know the number? Comment ✓ or ✕ 👇
Follow @fairorfault – your daily padel quiz.

posts.fact_source: FIP Reglamento de Juego, Regla 5.1 (cambio de campo cuando la suma de juegos es impar)

slides.claim: You switch sides after games 1, 3, 5 and so on.

slides.text: Game 1 is over. Time to switch?

scene.alt: Court from above with arrows showing both pairs changing ends

slides.line:
Switch when the games
add up to an **odd** number.

posts.caption:
Quick one for your next match ⏱️

When do you change ends in padel? After every game, every two games – or after the odd ones?

posts.fact_source: FIP Reglamento de Juego, Regla 13.1.e + Regla 16 (juego exterior: solo por lateral o puerta)

slides.q: Smash over the back glass. Can a pro run out and save it?
slides.claim: The smash flies over the back glass. A pro runs out and saves it.

slides.text: One bounce, then over the back glass.

scene.alt: Side view: the smash bounces once and flies over the opponents' back glass while a player runs

slides.line:
Over the back glass,
the point is **over**.

posts.caption:
You've seen pros sprint out of the court to save a smash. Unbelievable. 🤯

But can they do it when the ball flies over the BACK glass?

Make your call in the comments 👇
Follow @fairorfault – your daily padel quiz.

posts.fact_source: FIP Reglamento de Juego, Regla 12.3 (tras el bote, los elementos de la pista mantienen la pelota en juego)

slides.q: Side glass, then back glass. Still in play?
slides.claim: The ball bounces, hits the side glass, then the back glass. Still in play.

slides.text: It bounces, then side glass, then back glass.

scene.alt: Court from above: the ball bounces, hits the side glass, then the back glass

slides.line:
Walls after the bounce
keep the ball **in play**.

posts.caption:
Two walls in a row. Your partner already stopped running. 😅

Is the ball still alive after side glass AND back glass?

Comment FAIR or FAULT 👇 Send it to your partner.

posts.fact_source: FIP Reglamento de Juego, Regla 13.1.j (la pelota toca al propio jugador o a su compañero)

slides.q: Your shot hits your partner first. Still OK?
slides.claim: Your shot hits your partner, then goes over the net.

slides.text: Your shot touches your partner, then goes over.

scene.alt: Side view: the ball hits the partner's back and then flies over the net

slides.line:
The ball touched your team.
Point **lost**.

posts.caption:
It happens to everyone: you hit your partner with your own shot. 😬

But if the ball still goes over – does the point go on?

Comment FAIR or FAULT 👇 Tag the partner who got hit.

posts.fact_source: FIP Reglamento de Juego, Regla 9.1.a + 7.1.e (net solo si no toca la malla antes del segundo bote)

slides.q: Net, in the box, then the fence. Replay the serve?
slides.claim: Your serve clips the net, lands in, then hits the fence. You replay it.

slides.text: Net, in the box, then the fence.

scene.alt: Side view: the serve clips the net, bounces in the box and hits the fence

slides.line:
The fence turns it
into a **fault**.

posts.caption:
Net cord on the serve – everyone knows you just serve again. Right? 🤔

Not always. One detail changes everything.

posts.fact_source: FIP Reglamento de Juego, Regla 6.5 (al golpear, al menos un pie en contacto con el suelo, altura de la cintura)

slides.q: Can a pro serve with a jump, like in tennis?
slides.claim: A pro may jump when serving, like in tennis.

slides.text: Both feet off the ground at contact.

scene.alt: Side view: a player serves while jumping, both feet off the ground

slides.line:
One foot must stay
on the **ground**.

posts.caption:
Tennis players jump into their serve. Padel pros never do. 👀

Is it just style – or is it the rules?

Make your call in the comments 👇
